### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **128** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**70** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (30 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (35 routes)`, `routeManager (25 routes)`, `recordId (4 routes)`, `enforceApiAccess (12 routes)`, `resolveProtocol (29 routes)`
- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 44 pages)`, `/data/:object (route, 77 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c39a68c749eb31eb1b92add629bd33220d67f0eb` — the merge of head `b18b209442336a431e51c44587873c8f85e09145` into base `cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c39a68c749eb31eb1b92add629bd33220d67f0eb && git checkout c39a68c749eb31eb1b92add629bd33220d67f0eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10 b18b209442336a431e51c44587873c8f85e09145 && git checkout -B drift-repro cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10 && git merge --no-ff b18b209442336a431e51c44587873c8f85e09145

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cb7b3ccbc71ecbcf6bc8acea6478e74eec59ea10` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b5217d3fd646120ef44a6f29d5120f8a2b5c251`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts + packages/rest/src/recycle-bin-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/list.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/restore.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-writes.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx

Inputs read: card #30237 body and all 41 comments (consent 6721939207 S1–S3 = A; amendments 6721792971, 6721834323; hand-over 6690307585; rulings Q1–Q7, 6691358077, 6718336940, 6720657486), PR #31595 body and 34-file list, `git diff origin/main...pr-31595` at `2b5217d3`, the check-runs on `2b5217d3` (every required run `success`; the rest `skipped` by filter; none failed — Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check · workspace/consumer/source/debt, Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links all green). The rest of the diff (tests, census pins, `authorable-surface/api.json`, generated `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` register, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` re-exports, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the tree:

- **S1 `DeleteDataResponseSchema.recycleBinEntryId: z.string().optional()`** — a response-side widening; `authorable-surface/api.json` gains the one row and `references/api/protocol.mdx` the one table row (both regenerated). Right.
- **S3 `API_METHOD_DERIVATION.restore/purge = { all: ['delete'] }`** — the effective closure of every object exposing `delete` grows by two verbs. Consumers read in the live tree and each moves with it: `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` (REST 405 `allowed`, `rest-server.ts:584–592`), `canServeApiOperation` → core `annotateEffectiveApiOperations` (`/me/permissions`, re-pinned in `effective-object-permissions.test.ts` and plugin-hono-server `effective-api-operations.test.ts`), nav servability (asks `list`, unaffected). Core's `EXTERNAL_WRITE_GATED_OPERATIONS` already lists `restore`/`purge`, so the ADR-0015 Gate-3 clamp covers them without change. Right.
- **S2 not committed in spec** — `data-engine.zod.ts` is byte-identical to `main`; the out-channel is `RecycleBinDeleteObservability.onRecycleBinEntry` in objectql, intersected onto `ObjectQL.delete`'s options and admitted by `ENGINE_DELETE_OPTION_KEYS`. `HookDeleteOptions = Omit<EngineDeleteOptions, …>` therefore does not inherit it, so app-authored bodies are not told entry ids. Narrower than consent 6721939207, in the direction the consent allows; no spec parsed-alias moves. Right.
- **REST public surface**: four doors under `{data}/:object/recycle-bin` registered inside `api.enableCrud` ahead of the greedy `/:object/:id` (pinned); four `recycle-bin` ledger rows with `disposition: 'sdk'` and `client: recycleBin.*`, which the client implements; OpenAPI via `routeManager` metadata; `ApiRoutesSchema` unchanged (seat's call 6721834323). Right.
- **Wire delete answer**: `deleteData` adds `recycleBinEntryId` only when told; `crud-routes.ts:558` relays `res.json(result)` and the #28661 stale-summary path rides `withEarnedAnswer(stale, answer)`, so the key reaches the wire on both paths. Client `DeleteDataResult.recycleBinEntryId?` matches. Right.
- **objectql public surface**: `ObjectQL.listRecycleBin`, `RecycleBinListOptions/Result/ListedEntry`, `RecycleBinDeleteObservability`, `RECYCLE_BIN_LIST_{DEFAULT,MAX}_LIMIT`; `restore`/`purge` options gain `object`. All additive. Right.
- **System-context register**: row 29f for `assertCallerManagesRecycleBin` (the one new `isSystem` read). Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30237-recycle-bin-rest-doors.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, objectql / metadata-protocol / rest / client `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: new doors, a new optional response key, a larger derived exposure set; nothing is refused that was accepted. `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is right: an authored `apiMethods` whitelist that grants `delete` now means `restore`/`purge` are exposed too (a changed meaning of an accepted value; no key added or removed). Under AGENTS.md step 3 a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves and the protocol change lives in `@objectstack/spec`, so `minor` there and `patch` elsewhere is the rule's grading (non-protocol widenings ship `patch`); `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Both declaration lines appear line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. The `Skills-docs:` line cites #30847 as the card requires. Clause-②: `yes (widening)` — matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Claim-surface deviations (PR body, Acceptance notes)**: `packages/metadata-protocol` `deleteData`, `packages/client` `recycleBin.*` and `engine.ts` `listRecycleBin` are admitted by amendment 6721834323. Not named in any amendment: `api-derivation.test.ts`, the regenerated `protocol.mdx` / `api.json`, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`, the core and plugin-hono-server pin tests, `system-context.mdx` row 29f, `http-protocol.mdx`. Each is a test, a generator output or the prose the doors make true, inside the "tests, docs pages the doors make false" clause of 6721792971. Answered: in surface; the seat records them in one amendment line.
- **`Metadata-protocol: semantic` / spec `minor`** — answered in ②: right.
- **"A row the driver does not remove keeps its bin entry"** (dev out-of-scope finding, class b, "noted, not filed"): pre-existing since PR 1; this PR correctly withholds the id for `false`/`0` (pinned). Answered for this PR. Escalated: it should be a filed card, not a note — a bin entry snapshotting a row that is still live is a ghost entry an admin can see and try to restore (the id probe refuses it `RESTORE_UNIQUE_VALUE_TAKEN`, so no duplicate, but the entry is noise until the TTL reaps it). Seat files it.
- **S2 taken out of spec** — answered in ①: a narrowing of the dev's own consented scope; the maintainer need not be re-asked.
- **The list rides the `restore` exposure gate** — reasoned (there is no `list` verb on the bin in `ApiOperation`; the listing is the restore page's read). Accepted; the `recycle-bin-routes.ts` header says so.
- **Seat addition: a `sys_` object exposing `delete` is annotated `restore`/`purge` while the bin answers 400** — graded in ④ as nit + follow-up card, with the reasoning.
- **Not flagged by the dev, found here**: spec prose outside consent 6721939207 that S3 makes false (④, N2). The step-1 spec report should have named them; they go to a follow-up card.
- dev report `open_questions: []`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (S1)** against consent 6721939207 S1 and its first consumer. `deleteData` (`protocol-data-writes.ts`) hands the engine `onRecycleBinEntry` and spreads the key only when told; the engine tells it only from the by-id arm, only when `bin.write()` produced an entry and the driver's answer was neither `false` nor `0`, after the unit it opened has returned (`engine.ts` ~:9064–9108). So the key is present iff the answer's `success: true` and an entry exists to restore — exactly what a `POST …/recycle-bin/:entryId/restore` needs. A platform object, `multi`, `permanent` and a composition with no bin open no capture, so no id. Parsed against the schema in `protocol.delete-recycle-bin-entry.test.ts`. Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts` (S3)** against consent 6721939207 S3 and its first consumers. `isLegacyDerivable` with no `flag` reduces to `rule.all.every(...)`, so `restore`/`purge` follow `delete` exactly: unrestricted → present; `['get','list','create','update']` → absent; `[]` → absent (all pinned). The `isApiOperationAllowed` comment no longer claims a permanently-off flag. `enforceApiAccess` asks `'restore'` on the list and restore doors and `'purge'` on purge and empty, so the gate decision and the 405 `allowed` array come from the one table (pinned: 405 at all four doors when `delete` is withheld, no engine verb called). ADR-0148 D5's sentence that the *retired authored* `apiMethods` values `restore`/`purge` stay retired still holds: the authored enum is unchanged and `stripLegacyApiMethods` still strips them; only derivation moves, as the ruling says. Holds, with one prose nit (N1).

**Implementing files, sentence by sentence against the contract they implement:**

- `recycle-bin-routes.ts`: each door passes `enforceAuth`, the closed query set (`limit`/`offset` on the list, none on the acts; repeats refused), the exposure gate, then the engine as the caller. FLS on the list follows `ISecurityService.getQueryableFields`'s own contract (`security-service.ts:680–703`): queryable = readable minus masked; with no `getQueryableFields` every field declaring a `maskingRule` is withheld whoever asks; no answer → `id` alone; no service → values as stored; `clearedReferences` never served. The restore answer is a five-member receipt (#8497). `answerThrown` orders 503 (authz store) → 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` (declared paging) → sandbox fault → classified refusal with `REFUSAL_DETAIL_KEYS` (incl. `parentEntryId` for `RESTORE_PARENT_IN_RECYCLE_BIN`, `param` for the engine's 400) → 500 with text withheld. Agrees with the hand-over (list for managers, FLS on the live object, closed query sets) and the changeset's sentences.
- `rest-server.ts`: the host literal hands the module exactly the `RecycleBinRouteHost` members; registration sits inside `if (this.config.api.enableCrud)` before `registerDataActionEndpoints`, so the two-segment literals win over `/:object/:id` (mount-table pin updated).
- `list.ts`: platform object refused 400 before any permission is asked; paging bounds 1–200 / ≥0 refused 400 naming the param; `assertCallerManagesRecycleBin` fails closed (no resolver, throwing resolver, no entry for the object → 403) and exempts the system (row 29f); no bin → empty page; wall deny → empty page; the read is scoped through `buildDriverOptions(RECYCLE_BIN_OBJECT, context)` as `purge.ts` scopes; newest first, `limit + 1` for `hasMore`. Agrees with ADR-0148 D2 Permissions ("an admin sees all — lists every entry") and D5.
- `restore.ts` / `purge.ts`: `options.object` mismatch answers `null` / `false` before any dispatch (pinned); `callerRecycleBinManagement` is a pure refactor of the PR 4 check with its text kept; `recycleBinPlatformObjectRefusal` and `parseSnapshot` are exported unchanged in behaviour.
- `engine.ts` / `engine-top-level.ts`: the callback is a closure-free type intersection, admitted by `ENGINE_DELETE_OPTION_KEYS` with the drift pin updated; called once, after `result` is assigned, guarded by `typeof === 'function'`.
- `client/src/index.ts`: the four methods hit the ledger's exact paths with `encodeURIComponent` on both segments and `unwrapResponse`; `DeleteDataResult` gains the optional key. Types mirror the door's answers (nulls for absent entry fields, as the door sends them).
- `http-protocol.mdx`: the doors table, the who-may column (`manageRecycleBin` / `allowRestoreOwnDeleted`), the 404 for a mis-addressed entry, the four 409 codes and the `recycleBinEntryId` example agree with the code above. The retired "no recycle-bin runtime" warning is gone.

**Findings** (graded; none is a must-fix or should-fix):

- **N1 · nit (hits prose; follow-up card)** — `api-derivation.ts` docblock: "an object that exposes `delete` exposes its recycle bin's doors" overclaims for platform objects. ADR-0148 D5 excludes `sys_`/`cloud_`/`ai_` "by rule, not by a flag", so the exclusion is not an `enable` fact and the table (a pure function of `EnableLike`) cannot see it. Consequence in the tree: core `annotateEffectiveApiOperations` (read, not reviewed) lists `restore`/`purge` on a platform object that exposes `delete` — reachable today only through the super-user seeded closure, since no `sys_*` object on `main` restricts `apiMethods` to a set containing `delete` and an unrestricted object carries no annotation — while the doors answer `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (list/empty, `recycleBinPlatformObjectRefusal`) or `404` (restore/purge; no entry ever carries a platform `object_name`). **Grading**: the spec's own `apiOperations` describe (`permission.zod.ts:849`) promises `effectiveOperationsArray`'s closure, which this PR produces; door parity is core's #20135 refinement, whose pin covers eight `DOOR_OPERATIONS` that exclude `restore`/`purge`. No spec sentence is breached, nothing leaks (the bin holds no platform rows), the refusal is precise, and the only reader (#30239) does not exist yet. So a nit, not a should-fix. **Follow-up card**: core withholds `restore`/`purge` where `hasPlatformObjectPrefix(obj)` (the #30370 pattern: a refusal for every caller the table cannot see, folded at the annotation), the doors may answer 405 there for parity, and the hits docblock gains the clause "a platform object has no bin; the annotation withholds the two verbs there". Not fixed on this head: it would move code.
- **N2 · nit (prose outside the diff / outside consent; follow-up card)** — texts S3 (and PRs 1–3) make false, each outside consent 6721939207 so rightly untouched here, but unreported by the dev's step-1 spec report: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:84–85` `LEGACY_API_METHOD_GUIDANCE.restore/purge` ("never derives … returns only with a real recycle bin, and that soft-delete work is parked") — the author-facing twin of the table, printed by the strip warning; `object.zod.ts:1667` `softDelete` tombstone ("there is no soft-delete/recycle-bin runtime"); `packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts:31` (`undelete`: "no restore operation"); `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts:580` ("`restore` / `purge`, which never derive today"). A card in the shape of #31508 (prose only, `Clause-②: no`, spec consent for the two `packages/spec/src` files). `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md:414` and its eval are #30847's.
- **N3 · nit (accepted deviation)** — `engine.ts` comment "after the transaction commits, never from inside it": true of the unit this delete opens; inside a caller-held transaction on `context` the callback fires before the outer commit. The one producer-side caller, `deleteData`, holds none; in-process callers composing their own unit should read the id as provisional. No fix needed on this head.
- **N4 · nit (accepted deviation)** — `protocol.zod.ts` jsdoc lists why the key is absent (platform object, no bin, no entry id) but not the `success: false` case (driver answered `false`/`0`; an entry may exist but is not named). The describe's "absent when the delete wrote none" is the client-facing sentence and is safe; the jsdoc list is incomplete, not wrong.

Tried to break: an anonymous caller (401 before anything is listed, pinned); a caller with `allowDelete` but no manager bit (engine 403, pinned in `list.test.ts`); a repeated `?limit=` (400 before the gate); an entry addressed under another object (null/false → 404, no dispatch); a sandboxed hook fault on restore (answered as the data doors do); a stale roll-up after restore (200 with what was written); `onRecycleBinEntry` passed as a non-function from an in-process caller (ignored by the `typeof` guard); a wire body cannot carry a function, and `HookDeleteOptions` does not inherit the key.

队列构建 [42506290340](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42506290340) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42506290340/job/128809649541)** — 失败步骤: Boot example apps and exercise real user flows

  ```

    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: UNCLASSIFIED surface — add a ledger row (ADR-0060): rest-family:rest-route-ledger.ts:recycle-bin: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []
  ```
